title: Man shot dead: SQ remained on scene to secure the area
article: Man shot dead: the Sûreté du Québec remained on scene to secure the area.
A 41-year-old man died during a police operation in Beauceville.
Quebec's independent investigations bureau (BEI) says it was appropriate for the SQ to stay on site for several hours to protect a wide security perimeter before BEI investigators arrived.

According to BEI spokesperson Martin Bonin-Charron, it is the responsibility of the police service already present to ensure the safety and integrity of the scene and to take reasonable measures to prevent involved or witness officers from speaking to each other about the event.
A 911 call was made around 9:45 a.m. Monday regarding a domestic-violence incident at a home on Route du Golf in Beauceville.

When officers arrived shortly before 11 a.m., Emmanuel Therrien, 41, allegedly moved his hand toward a weapon he was wearing at his belt, and officers opened fire. He was fatally struck by at least one rifle round.

Eight BEI investigators reached the scene around 5 p.m. and left early Tuesday around 3 a.m.; the BEI is based in Longueuil, and geography is taken into account in the rules governing independent investigations.
BEI regulations call for interviews with involved officers within 48 hours of investigators' arrival and with witness officers within 24 hours; the organization's budget was $4 million for 2016-2017.
Emmanuel Therrien, a father of three originally from Sainte-Anne-des-Monts in the Gaspé, had lived with his family in the Beauceville area for about five years and was appreciated by neighbors.
